note: Report excellent: 17 findings, correctly separated load-bearing ledgers from drift, auditable clean-file list. Edits rejected: mechanical s/now/should/ demoted three TRUE shipped-state claims (levelMin/levelMax in troop.lua + validator_core.lua + map-editor.js) into pending work, and inverted the encounterSteps gap statement into design intent. Lesson: 'find X' delegates well, 'fix X' needs the delegate to verify each claim against code first -- which the brief did not require.

Measurement task ('find X'), the class the n=1 row predicted would delegate well. It did. Headline finding correct and independently verified: 0 sealed faces is real, because viewport_3d.lua:1335 addFace returns early when the neighbour is a wall, so the resolved face list excludes wall-to-wall adjacency by construction. Remaining win is exterior-only, 916/2518 = 36.38% across 13/13 maps, none skipped. Classifier's sealed branch is genuinely exercised by tests rather than a dead path returning zero, and the opening-adjacency negative control (visually enclosed but must be visible) is the correct control and works. Two defects found in review: ceilingQuads derives #structure.floorCells so it counts walkable cells rather than emitted quads (map_renderable_bundle has three ceiling paths, only one is addQuad); and renderable_bundle.collect() is asserted then discarded, which is both wasted work and the natural fix for the first defect. One false claim: reported a 'pre-existing test_map_geometry_export crash' and refused to claim the unit gate green because of it. The refusal was exactly right discipline; the premise was wrong. A clean main worktree gives ALL UNIT TESTS OK. The crash was filesystem contention from working inside the primary checkout, same root cause as the .git/index.lock permission denial it also hit. Worktree isolation was not followed, but the preamble did not require it at the time - that gap was ours, closed by #298. Lesson: goal mode suits bounded measurement with deterministic verification. Its weak point is environmental attribution - it cannot tell a collision from a pre-existing defect, so any baseline claim it makes needs re-measuring on a clean tree.

Measurement task in goal mode, and the strongest delegated run so far. Followed the worktree isolation rule added in #298 -- primary checkout stayed clean on main, which is direct evidence that fix works. Five repeats per configuration with raw samples retained, min/median/max per span, spans reported separately rather than aggregated. Result verified independently: map 8 median loadToFirstUsableMs 885.08 -> 288.49 ms, a 596.59 ms improvement against a 62.66 ms baseline spread, with every staged sample below every baseline sample. Correctly declined to claim GPU materialization or transform speedups, both of which moved within their own spreads. The negative control fired and was diagnosed rather than papered over: staged map 12 showed zero prebake.deserialize, and the run traced it to tileset dungeon_ffxii_depth_explore having no heightMap, so the map is a genuine uncovered control rather than a silent load failure. I confirmed that independently. This also revealed that PR #295's own suggested comparison nominates a map its prebake cannot cover. Also handled two environment problems honestly: a stdout pipe backpressure timeout in its own harness (discarded those runs, documented the correction) and a blank Start-Process exit code (fell back to asserting positive profile markers, exactly as the preamble requires). Recorded the exporter's missing GEOMETRY PREBAKE OK marker as an anomaly rather than repairing it, which was correct for a measurement task. Only gap: did not quantify how narrow the coverage is -- 3 of 14 tilesets are height-authored, and the slowest map measured is the uncovered one, with ~1.7s of QEM outside the prebake's scope. That was not asked for, so it is a note rather than a fault. Lesson: goal mode is at its best on bounded measurement where the brief supplies both the repetition requirement and a negative control. Both additions earned their place here.

Labour was correct; the brief was wrong. It did exactly what was asked, deterministically, with real tests, and it shrank the baseline by exactly the eight entries that stopped reproducing rather than rewriting it. Every ring is a true annulus with UVs and the gate goes green. But the cohort is eight variations of one ring: top IoU pair 0.9616 against a 0.97 threshold, six pairs above 0.91. Root cause is mine, not the delegate's -- a ring's defining feature is a gem at one point on the band, which is not rotationally symmetric, so a pure lathe can only ever raise a rim around the whole circumference. Rings were the wrong first cohort for this primitive. Lesson: a mechanically-graded brief makes a cheap agent reliable at hitting the grader, which means a permissive grader or an ill-matched primitive produces confident, well-tested, near-identical output. The delegate cannot catch a bad premise and should not be expected to.

Produced no diff. Stopped at a genuine runtime blocker (bounded_lane had no per-transfer arrival position) and correctly refused to edit runtime as instructed, but never resumed after reporting it. The recon was valuable and accurate - it found that map 8 already exits to map 1 and that PORTAL_TO_TOWN resolves through system.spawn - so the run paid for itself as a survey. As implementation it did not. Confirms the standing pattern: 'find X' delegates, 'fix X' does not.

Produced no diff, and could not have. The brief pointed at docs/design/st-maria-corner-grammar.md as the contract, but that file landed in c57a4220, which is LATER than this run's base of cbb91216 -- so the document genuinely did not exist in its worktree. It reported exactly that, and correctly reported the second blocker too: the requested pytest command did not start because PowerShell had no `python` on PATH. Both reports were accurate and checkable, and I confirmed both independently. Root cause is mine, not the delegate's: a brief cannot cite a document that postdates the base it is run against. Its status write-up (st-maria-body-sweep-handoff.md) is a snapshot of a stale worktree -- it says body.py is still the original rectilinear cell-complex builder, which was true at cbb91216 and would read later as a claim about the current grammar -- so it is not kept. Lesson: pin the brief and the base to the same commit, and check that every path the brief names resolves IN the worktree the delegate will get, not in the primary checkout.
